# Module `lune_ui_core::widgets::toolbar`

[API reference](../../INDEX.md) / parent [`lune_ui_core::widgets`](../widgets.md)

A strip of actions over a glass layer the app passes in (`widget.toolbar`).

[`Ui::toolbar`](../ui.md#method.Ui.toolbar) draws the bar and hands its three columns to the caller, who places the
actions: [`Ui::toolbar_action`](../ui.md#method.Ui.toolbar_action) (a 40 by 40 glyph button with a tooltip) and
[`Ui::toolbar_label`](../ui.md#method.Ui.toolbar_label) (a glyph and an elided text, the branch button's shape). The commands and
their names are the app's. The bar is the app's glass layer, whatever the window's state (R13): the
widget names no preset, the caller passes the layer.

The columns are the entry's `*, Auto, *` grid. The middle column's width is the caller's
content, which this widget cannot know before the closure runs, so [`ToolbarCols::center`](toolbar.md#structfield.ToolbarCols.center) is
the zero-width rect at the middle: a centred group is placed around `center.x`, and the left
and right columns each run from the edge to that middle.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/widgets/toolbar.rs:1`

What [`Ui::toolbar`](../ui.md#method.Ui.toolbar) is given besides its rect.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/widgets/toolbar.rs:43`

**Fields**

- <a id="structfield.ToolbarOptions.glass"></a>`pub glass: GlassLayer`

  The glass layer the bar draws.

- <a id="structfield.ToolbarOptions.under"></a>`pub under: [f32; 4]`

  What the glass layer is composed over (the colour below it, premultiplied).
  Pass the layer the bar sits on: acrylic replaces what is under it, and the pixel just outside
  the rect takes this colour, so a zero `under` leaves a 1 px transparent rim over anything but
  the window edge.

- <a id="structfield.ToolbarOptions.name"></a>`pub name: &'a str`

  The accessible name of the bar.
